The fog bank moves at a constant speed, covering 3 miles of the city every 10 minutes. This gives a speed of 0.3 miles per minute. The city is 42 miles across from the oceanfront to the inland edge. To cover the whole city, the leading edge of the fog bank must travel the entire 42 miles. The time required is distance divided by speed: 42 miles / (3 miles / 10 minutes) = 140 minutes.

The note warns that some solvers mistakenly double the answer, likely by thinking the fog bank must completely pass over the city (i.e., its trailing edge must also reach the inland edge), which would take 84 miles and 280 minutes. However, "cover the whole city" means the city is fully engulfed in fog, which happens when the leading edge reaches the inland edge, assuming the fog bank is large enough.

Answer: 140
